world.setting: Chamberlain, Maine in the mid-1970s: austere suburban New England high school and suffocating domestic religious interiors.
world.register: austere, gritty 1970s American realism with claustrophobic domestic dread and catastrophic fire aftermath

carrie.name: Carrie White
carrie.role: Traumatized, telekinetic high school outcast pushed beyond endurance by abuse and public cruelty.
carrie.look: A sixteen-year-old girl with pale skin, awkward slumped posture, unruly mousy brown hair, plain shapeless home-sewn 1970s dress, and intense frightened blue eyes.

margaret.name: Margaret White
margaret.role: Fanatical fundamentalist mother enforcing religious terror and self-mutilating dogma.
margaret.look: A severe 45-year-old woman with gaunt features, tight graying bun, high-collared dark Victorian-style 1970s dress, and clutching a worn Bible with manic intensity.

sue.name: Sue Snell
sue.role: Remorseful popular senior attempting moral restitution by offering her prom date to Carrie.
sue.look: An attractive seventeen-year-old girl with blonde feathered 1970s hair, clean-cut preppy pastel sweater and plaid skirt, bearing a pensive and guilty expression.

tommy.name: Tommy Ross
tommy.role: Charismatic high school athlete and class president who genuinely respects Carrie at the prom.
tommy.look: A tall, athletic seventeen-year-old boy with wavy brown 1970s hair, friendly open smile, wearing a powder-blue tuxedo with dark velvet lapels.

chris.name: Chris Hargensen
chris.role: Vindictive, wealthy ringleader whose humiliation drives her to execute the pig blood prank.
chris.look: A sharply styled seventeen-year-old girl with manicured dark hair, entitled posture, fashionable 1970s silk blouse, and a cold mocking glare.

billy.name: Billy Nolan
billy.role: Violent delinquent boyfriend who procures the pig blood and enacts sociopathic hostility.
billy.look: An aggressive nineteen-year-old hoodlum with greasy black hair, denim jacket over white undershirt, cigarette behind ear, and callous smirking gaze.

classroom.look: A drab 1970s Maine public high school gymnasium and locker room with institutional brick walls, wooden benches, and metal lockers.

bedroom.look: The oppressive White household interior, featuring a claustrophobic prayer closet, blue-eyed bleeding crucifix, and heavy faded floral wallpaper.

stage.look: The decorated Ewen High prom stage with crepe paper gondolas, sparkling streamers, mirror ball, and the fateful suspended buckets above the coronation throne.

street.look: The nocturnal streets of Chamberlain engulfed in fire, ruptured fire hydrants, snapped power lines sparking violently, and exploding gas stations.

abstract.look: A clean documentarian inquiry space representing official Senate transcripts, psychiatric autopsies, and teletype news wires.

objects.why: Ewen High School social hierarchy and the institutional setting of the locker room and prom.
Domestic religious imprisonment, closet altar, and mental subjugation imposed by Margaret White.
The catastrophic conflagration that incinerates Chamberlain during Carrie's telekinetic retribution.
The mass casualties, memorial stones, and official death toll of over 400 victims.
Billy Nolan's hot rod vehicle used in the pig blood sabotage and the fatal confrontation.
The epistolary documentation, AP teletype news wires, Senate committee transcripts, and memoirs.
Carrie discovering her telekinesis and shattered self-image in the bathroom mirror.
The locked gymnasium fire exits sealing students inside during the prom disaster.

spine.claim: The tragedy begins not with demonic fury but with severe locker room cruelty and religious abuse manufacturing Carrie's deep isolation.
Institutional failure and misplaced guilt converge as Sue offers her prom date while Chris plots venomous revenge.
At the prom, a brief taste of genuine dignity is destroyed by the bucket prank, snapping Carrie's fragile restraint.
Telekinetic destruction turns Chamberlain into an inferno as Carrie exacts indiscriminate retribution across the town.
The epistolary autopsy leaves a haunting societal warning that institutional neglect weaponizes the vulnerable into devastating catastrophe.
